nodes.summary: CLIQUE COVER is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a clique-cover instance that is both well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The CLIQUE COVER decision problem

nodes.summary: A clique-cover instance $(n, E, \ell)$ is feasible when there is a map $c$ from the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ to $\{0, \dots, \ell - 1\}$ such that any two distinct vertices with the same value are adjacent in the graph of the instance. Each class of $c$ is then a clique, so the vertex set is the union of $\ell$ or fewer cliques, which is Karp's condition; conversely a cover by at most $\ell$ cliques can be shrunk…
nodes.title: Feasible clique-cover instances

nodes.summary: An instance of CLIQUE COVER is a triple $(n, E, \ell)$: a vertex count $n$, a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, and a natural number $\ell$, the bound on the number of cliques.
nodes.title: A clique-cover instance

nodes.summary: The CLIQUE COVER decision problem lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it. Recorded as wanted.
nodes.title: CLIQUE COVER is NP-complete

nodes.summary: The graph of a clique-cover instance $(n, E, \ell)$ is the simple graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ in which $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $u \ne v$ and $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ is listed in $E$.
nodes.title: The graph of a clique-cover instance

nodes.summary: A clique-cover instance $(n, E, \ell)$ is well formed when $E$ has no repeated entry and every listed pair $(u, v)$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, with $(v, u)$ not also listed. These are the conditions used for GRAPH COLORING instances in the repository.
nodes.title: Well-formed clique-cover instances

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.
